title: Sectionwise reconstruction on the identical underlying sheaf
statement: Let C be a category with a Grothendieck topology J and let R be an internal commutative ring object in sheaves of sets, in a universe at least as large as both universes of C. There is a sheaf A of commutative rings and an equality h from the underlying sheaf of R to the underlying-set sheaf of A. On every section set, transport along h preserves addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one.

source.place: Section 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), proof of Proposition 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), rings as sextuples

proof.text: Define the five operations on each original section set by evaluating the five internal operation morphisms. Evaluation of AddMonObj.add_assoc, zero_add, add_zero, IsCommAddMonObj.add_comm and AddGrpObj.left_neg gives an additive commutative group. Evaluation of MonObj.mul_assoc, one_mul, mul_one and IsCommMonObj.mul_comm gives a commutative monoid. Evaluation of RingObj.mul_add and add_mul gives distributivity; additive cancellation implies absorption by zero. These structures give a commutative ring, with recursive natural and integer scalar multiplication.

Keep every original restriction function. Naturality of the addition, multiplication, zero and one morphisms shows that it is a ring homomorphism. The original presheaf identity and composition laws give the ring-presheaf functor laws by concrete homomorphism extensionality. Thus the underlying-set presheaf is the original presheaf, definitionally up to its proof fields.

Use Mathlib limit-size shrinking to obtain limits and preservation in the site universes. Since the commutative-ring forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, reflectsLimits_of_reflectsIsomorphisms makes it reflect the required limits. Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp then lifts the given set-sheaf condition to the constructed ring presheaf.

Bundle this ring presheaf with its sheaf proof. The underlying sheaf equality is reflexivity, with proof irrelevance for the sheaf and functor laws. The transported addition, negation and multiplication equations are reflexivity. The zero and one equations follow by eliminating the unique section of the tensor unit. No arbitrary witness is chosen.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof of the sectionwise reconstruction part of the Stacks sextuple argument; no sorry.

lean.statement: theorem sheafRingObject_sectionwise_reconstruction {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : CommRingObjCat (Sheaf J (Type (max u v w)))) : ∃ (A : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v w}) (h : R.X = (sheafCompose J (forget CommRingCat.{max u v w})).obj A), ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ), (∀ a b : R.X.obj.obj U, (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U ((AddMonObj.add (X := R.X)).hom.app U (a, b)) = (show A.obj.obj U from (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U a) + (show A.obj.obj U from (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U b)) ∧ (∀ t : (𝟙_ (Sheaf J (Type (max u v w)))).obj.obj U, (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U ((AddMonObj.zero (X := R.X)).hom.app U t) = (0 : A.obj.obj U)) ∧ (∀ a : R.X.obj.obj U, (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U ((AddGrpObj.neg (X := R.X)).hom.app U a) = -(show A.obj.obj U from (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U a)) ∧ (∀ a b : R.X.obj.obj U, (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U ((MonObj.mul (X := R.X)).hom.app U (a, b)) = (show A.obj.obj U from (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U a) * (show A.obj.obj U from (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U b)) ∧ (∀ t : (𝟙_ (Sheaf J (Type (max u v w)))).obj.obj U, (eqToIso h).hom.hom.app U ((MonObj.one (X := R.X)).hom.app U t) = (1 : A.obj.obj U))
